title: Historical RTEC AAP disability and protected-veteran self-identification workflow

populations.historical_basis: Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act as stated in the source
invitation_characteristics: The source states refusal to provide the information will not result in adverse treatment.
An individual may identify at the time of invitation or later.
The source connects the information to affirmative-action inclusion, placement and accommodation.

populations.historical_basis: VEVRAA as stated in the source
invitation_characteristics: The source describes recently separated, other protected, Armed Forces service medal and disabled-veteran categories.
The source states refusal to provide the information will not result in adverse treatment.
Disabled-veteran information may also be used to identify needed accommodation.

historical_confidentiality_controls: Disability/veteran self-identification information is described as confidential.
Managers/supervisors may receive work-restriction or accommodation information when needed.
First-aid/safety personnel may receive information when and to the extent appropriate for emergency treatment.
Government officials enforcing applicable laws may receive information as described in the source.
The AAP itself was described as available for employee/applicant inspection through Human Resources.
privacy_boundary_for_agent_os: Completed self-identification forms and person-level disability/veteran status are restricted sensitive HR data.
Do not store completed self-identification responses, identities, disability details, veteran details or accommodation facts in generalized GitHub knowledge.
Generalized knowledge may retain blank-form structure, historical workflow, confidentiality rules, aggregate AAP counts and source provenance.
Restricted demographic source data may be used to compute approved aggregate reports, but only the aggregate result should enter the general compliance library.
currentness_warning: This record preserves historical AAP language through June 2024. It is not a current self-identification form or current legal instruction.
The historical source contains detailed definitions and statutory language that must not be copied into a present-day applicant/employee form without current review.
The source names Tracy Champion as a historical EEO contact; current EEO assignment is governed by the later signed 2026 EEO policy.
process_model: Provide the applicable approved self-identification invitation separately from qualification/hiring decisions.
Make participation voluntary and protect against adverse treatment for non-response, consistent with the governing current form/policy.
Store responses in restricted compliance data separated from ordinary decision-making data.
Use authorized aggregate outputs for AAP/EEO analysis.
Route accommodation requests through the current accommodation process rather than treating self-identification alone as an accommodation case.
Version the invitation/form and retain the source/effective period used for each reporting cycle.
unresolved_questions: What current approved disability self-identification form/process does RTEC use after June 2024?
